sentences.text: Ms. Sharmila Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal, learned Government Advocate for t  respondent(s) / State.

Heard on I.A. No.10794/2025, which is a repeat (second) application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant - Amar Singh @ Amriya S/o Badrilal

First application of the appellant (I.A.
No.10800/2025) was dismissed on merit vide order dated 25.11.2024.

The present appellant has been convicted for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363,
366, 376(2)(N), 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code & Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to under 03 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.200/-, 10 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.200/-, 10 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.200/-, 20 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.200/- and 20 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.200/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Counsel for the appellant argued mainly on the ground that the appellant has remained in jail for 03 years and 11 months.
She argued that 2 CRA-14782-2023 this is an appeal of 2023 and final hearing of the same may take time.
Hence, remaining jail sentence of the present appellant be suspended.
Counsel for the State has opposed the application by submitting that earlier application of the appellant was considered and rejected on merit.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact and evidence, we find that the prosecutrix was the consenting party and remained with the present appellant for about 1  months without any resistance and the basis on which the age of the prosecutrix was recorded in the scholar register has not been proved by the prosecution.
Hence, we deem it expedient to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.
